key_insight: A frozen unified multimodal model can be steered into a medical image segmenter by framing segmentation as structured visual generation and adding retrieval, sampling, and critique tools.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support training-free adaptation to new medical segmentation tasks where dense annotations are scarce and domain shift is common.
method: Uses a frozen unified multimodal model as the core generator for mask prediction
Adds Anatomy-Aware Knowledge Retrieval with in-context exemplars to inject anatomical guidance
Uses repeated sampling plus Comparative Quality Critique and iterative editing to refine masks
evidence_signal: Across eight medical segmentation datasets, SegBanana reports an average mDice of 77.45%, beating generalist and medical-specific baselines by at least 14.93 points and staying robust to out-of-domain visual supports.
watch_item: Performance still depends on the quality of retrieved visual supports and may remain weaker on cases requiring highly specialized anatomical or domain-specific knowledge.
paper_title: SegBanana: Steering Unified Multimodal Models into Medical Segmenters
